issues.description: Silent semantic change: identity now coerces non-numeric domain values to numbers, but coerceNumber maps null/undefined/NaN to 0
issues.detail: The original panLinear/zoomLinear used identity as ground and toNumber as lift, so non-numeric inputs propagated as null. The new coerceNumber returns 0 on null. This is an unreasoned substitution of behavior for the sake of satisfying the TransformFn signature. State the postcondition for non-numeric inputs; do not pick zero by accident.

issues.description: panLog/zoomLog read domain[0] before the non-emptiness guard, defeating the invariant
issues.detail: Math.sign(domain[0]) executes outside pan/zoom, so an empty domain passed to panLog yields Math.sign(undefined) = NaN before the guard ever fires. The precondition 'domain is non-empty' is asserted in the wrong place. Hoist the check to each public entry, or assert it before computing sign.

issues.description: Parameter type number[] contradicts the asserted invariant NonEmptyArray<T>
issues.detail: Public signatures advertise domain: number[] but the body refines via isNonEmpty. The type system already supports the stronger precondition; declaring it on the boundary would make the contract checkable by the caller rather than discovered at runtime. The current shape is tested-not-proved at the type level.

issues.description: Tests assert presence of error for panLinear/zoomLinear only; the other six entry points are unproved
issues.detail: panLog, panPow, panSymlog, zoomLog, zoomPow, zoomSymlog all share the same empty-domain precondition but no test exercises it. Two tests do not establish the invariant for eight functions. This is exactly the testing-shows-presence trap: the absent tests do not show absence of the bug, especially given the panLog/zoomLog sign issue above.

issues.description: peek overload claims T for non-empty tuple but the implementation cannot prove it
issues.detail: The new overload peek<T>(readonly [T, ...T[]]): T relies on array[array.length - 1] never being undefined. With noUncheckedIndexedAccess enabled this would not type-check. The overload is a type-level promise the implementation does not formally discharge; it is correct in practice but unreasoned at the level the overload pretends to operate.

review.summary: The refactor is largely a faithful type annotation of working code, which is fine as far as it goes. However, the empty-domain precondition is asserted inconsistently: panLog/zoomLog read domain[0] before the guard, so the invariant fails for the very functions that need it most. A second unreasoned change hides inside coerceNumber, which silently maps null/undefined to 0 where the original returned null — a postcondition shift introduced for typing convenience. Tests cover only two of eight entry points for the new error path; this is tested-not-proved. Verdict: REASONED in skeleton, UNREASONED at the boundaries that matter. Fix the guard placement and document the coercion choice before merge.
